name: Slack
summary: Easy to create, easy to install in one workspace. Installing in other customers' workspaces needs distribution turned on. A public Marketplace listing is an optional, discretionary review with a usage floor. Beware: the discovery document on slack.com describes Sign in with Slack only, not app installs.

difficulty.label: Easy to moderate
difficulty.why: Self-serve for unlisted distribution. Marketplace review is optional but has requirements and no published timeline.

time.wait: None for unlisted distribution. Marketplace review time is not published.
time.total: Same day for private use. Weeks plausible for Marketplace (unverified).

approval.type: None to install; Marketplace review optional
approval.detail: Marketplace apps are checked against guidelines and installed and tested by the team. The team may deny any app. Minimum usage: 10 active workspaces and 20 monthly active users.

endpoints.discovery: slack.com/.well-known/openid-configuration exists but covers Sign in with Slack (openid, profile, email) only. Do not use it for app installs.

agentCan: Generate the app manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, event subscriptions) so you can create the app from a paste
Build the authorize URL and the oauth.v2.access exchange
Review your requested scopes and flag any you do not use, since unused scopes are a listed reason Marketplace submissions get returned
Draft the Marketplace listing copy and a security checklist
youMustDo: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps under a workspace you control
Activate public distribution in the app settings
Submit for Marketplace review yourself, and respond to reviewers quickly

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps choose Create New App. Starting from a manifest is faster and reviewable in a PR.

steps.title: Configure redirect URLs and scopes
steps.detail: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS, cannot contain an anchor (#), and your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured URL. With several URLs configured, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and access steps, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri.

steps.title: Choose bot vs user scopes
steps.detail: Bot tokens come from oauth.v2.access. A user-token flow also exists (oauth.v2.user.access). Request the minimum scopes.

steps.title: Enable distribution
steps.detail: Undistributed apps can only be installed on the workspace where they were created. Distribution settings live under Manage Distribution in app settings. The oauth doc did not describe the steps, so confirm against the distribution docs.

steps.title: Consider token rotation
steps.detail: Available for apps using granular permissions: tokens are exchanged for a refresh token plus expiring access token. Without rotation, tokens do not expire.

steps.title: Optional: Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Needs a policy-compliant app, a quality listing, and prompt support (a reply within 2 business days). Expect the team to install and test it. Security: use the state parameter, TLS 1.2+, verify request signatures, store tokens securely.

requirements: Slack workspace where you can create apps
For Marketplace: at least 10 active workspaces and 20 monthly active users, a support channel, and compliant branding

gotchas.detail: An agent that probes /.well-known on slack.com finds a valid OIDC document, but its endpoints are for Sign in with Slack and will not install your app.
The team may deny any app. Mismatched images, unused scopes and substantial feature changes can trigger a return or resubmission.
The guidelines page defers to a separate review guide, which was not read in this run.
You need 10 active workspaces before you can list publicly, so unlisted distribution has to carry you there.

blockers.fix: Make redirect_uri identical in the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls when more than one URL is configured.
A scope you request is not yet approved for the listing. Request only approved scopes or resubmit with the new one.
A workspace admin must approve it (recalled behavior, not verified in this run).
